newsitem.title: ITALY: Two more mountaineers die in Italian Alps.
newsitem.headline: Two more mountaineers die in Italian Alps.

text.p: An Italian man in his 60s died on Monday after falling while climbing in the eastern Alps with his son, rescue officials said.
Pio Bertamini, 67, fell several metres (yards) after slipping while scaling a 2,757 metre (9,190 foot) peak. He hit his head on rocks and was dead by the time rescuers reached him.
Hospital officials said on Monday that another Italian climber, 27-year-old Antonio Silverstri, who tumbled into a cravass in the eastern Alps on Sunday, had died of his injuries.

More than 50 climbers have died in a rash of climbing accidents in Europe's highest mountain range over the past two weeks. Experts say heavy snowfalls in June combined with rising temperatures have made conditions treacherous.
Officials say more than 30 climbers have died in the Italian Alps since the start of the main summer climbing season in July.
